title: Priority hotpatch for heterogeneous token surge causing cross-env TTFT regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: On 2026-03-09 we began receiving multiple customer escalations reporting elevated TTFT and reduced tokens/sec for generation endpoints across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. This ticket tracks the urgent diagnostic and mitigation work: triage, hotpatch design, staged rollout, verification and customer communications. The regression presents as 2-5x increase in first-token latency for mid-length (128-512 tokens) requests for a subset of quantized model variants and appears more severe under mixed workload multiplexing. Customer traffic patterns that exercise heterogeneous model fanout expose a kernel-selection / KV-prefetch race that causes repeated context rehydration and micro-batching stalls.
impact_summary: Impacted customers include two enterprise Dedicated customers and three Hosted tenants (high-volume chatapps). Median TTFT increase from ~40ms to ~220ms for affected paths; tokens/sec per-worker dropped by ~30-60% at peak. SLOs breached for affected routes; several paid customers escalated to SEV2. Incidents observed in US and EU regions; Private on-prem installs reported similar symptom with internal scheduler config.
root_cause_analysis: Preliminary root-cause: an interaction between the kernel selector heuristic and adaptive KV prefetcher. For certain quantized kernels (int8 fallback path) the selector chose a memory-efficient kernel that increases context-copy latency for mid-length sequences. At the same time the KV-prefetcher aggressively prefetches model shards for predicted fanout, but a race during multiplexed request assembly caused prefetch cancellations and repeated rehydrations of the KV cache. The combined effect is repeated micro-batch backpressure and kernel switch thrashing, increasing first-token latency and decreasing sustained tokens/sec.
mitigation_applied: Fast mitigation implemented 2026-03-11: 1) Temporarily pinned kernel-selection policy to prefer low-latency kernels for quantized variants in hosted and dedicated pools, 2) Added conservative backoff to KV-prefetcher to avoid aggressive prefetch during multiplex bursts, 3) Deployed per-route short-term rate cap for affected tenants and enabled hedged warmstarts for high-priority keys. Hotpatch rolled to staging, Canary (5% traffic), and then 40% within 2 hours. Initial telemetry shows median TTFT improvement to ~65ms in Canary and tokens/sec recovery of ~80% of baseline.
